new.s: Who can remove the Chairman of a State Public Service Commission?
new.x: The Governor appoints the SPSC Chairman, but only the President can remove him under Article 317.

new.s: Up to what age does the Chairman of the UPSC hold office?
new.x: UPSC members hold office for six years or till 65; for SPSC and JSPSC members the limit is 62.

new.s: Which of the following is called the central recruiting agency of India?
new.x: The UPSC, an independent constitutional body under Article 315, is the central recruiting agency of India.

new.s: Which committee reviewed the Civil Services Examination in 2001?
new.x: The Y.K. Alagh Committee (2001) reviewed the Civil Services Examination and suggested an aptitude test.

new.s: Who headed the committee of 2015-16 that reviewed the age limit and pattern of the Civil Services Examination?
new.x: The B.S. Baswan Committee (2015-16) reviewed the age limit and pattern of the Civil Services Examination.

new.s: In which year was the Andhra Public Service Commission, a predecessor of the APPSC, set up?
new.x: The Andhra PSC was set up in 1953; it merged with the Hyderabad PSC to form the APPSC on 1 November 1956.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the advice of the UPSC:
1. Consultation with the UPSC is mandatory, and action taken without it is invalid.
2. The advice of the UPSC is only advisory.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Consultation is directory, not mandatory, so action without it is not invalid for that reason alone; the advice is only advisory.

new.s: N.K. Singh was the Chairman of which Finance Commission?
new.x: N.K. Singh chaired the 15th Finance Commission (2020-21 and 2021-26).

new.s: Which Finance Commission was headed by C. Rangarajan?
new.x: C. Rangarajan chaired the 12th Finance Commission (2005-10).

new.s: Which Finance Commission recommended a 29.5% share for the States in Central taxes?
new.x: The 11th Finance Commission (A.M. Khusro) recommended 29.5%; the 12th raised it to 30.5%.
new.angle: U0344 #3 share of central taxes -> FC

new.s: What was the award period of the first Finance Commission chaired by K.C. Neogy?
new.x: The first Finance Commission under K.C. Neogy covered 1952-57.

new.s: Who was the Chairman of the 5th Finance Commission, on whose recommendation Special Category Status was introduced in 1969?
new.x: Special Category Status was introduced in 1969 on the recommendation of the 5th Finance Commission headed by Mahavir Tyagi.

new.s: By which formula were funds allotted to Special Category States?
new.x: Funds for Special Category States were allotted by the Gadgil formula approved by the NDC.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the 14th Finance Commission:
1. It raised the States' share from 32% to 42%, the largest increase ever.
2. It made no distinction between special and general category States.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The 14th FC made the largest ever rise (32% to 42%) and did not distinguish special and general category States.

new.s: Under the Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951, which of the following is NOT a qualification for a member?
o: A High Court judge or one qualified to be one
Special knowledge of government finance and accounts
Membership of Parliament for ten years
new.x: The 1951 Act lists a High Court judge, finance and accounts, financial administration and economics; Parliament membership is not a qualification.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the members of the Finance Commission:
1. The Constitution fixes their term at five years.
2. They are eligible for reappointment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The term is what the President specifies, not fixed by the Constitution, and members can be reappointed.
new.angle: U0344 notes: FC term and reappointment

new.s: Who among the following, as Chairman of the 4th Finance Commission, held that its recommendations should not be rejected without very compelling reasons?
new.x: P.V. Rajamannar of the 4th Finance Commission said its recommendations should not be rejected without very compelling reasons.

new.s: In which year was the 15th Finance Commission constituted?
new.x: The 15th Finance Commission was formed on 27 November 2017 under N.K. Singh.

new.s: Who grants or refuses leave to the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?
new.x: Leave of the CAG is granted or refused by the President.

new.s: To whom does the Comptroller and Auditor General of India address his resignation?
new.x: The CAG is appointed by the President and resigns to the President.

new.s: Which of the following offices has the same term of office as the CAG, that is, six years or till the age of 65?
o: Member of a State Public Service Commission
new.x: The CAG and the CEC both hold office for six years or till 65; an SPSC member retires at 62 and the President has five years.
new.angle: U0345 #10 term compared with other posts

new.s: Which of the following is a unitary feature of the Indian Constitution?
o: Office of the CAG auditing both Union and State accounts
new.x: A single CAG audits the accounts of both the Union and the States, which is a unitary feature; the others are federal features.
new.angle: U0345 APPSC PYQ y127d06012d5 CAG as non-federal feature

new.s: On whose request does the CAG audit the accounts of local bodies?
new.x: The CAG audits local bodies only when the President or the Governor requests it.

new.s: Which of the following is audited by private auditors on the CAG's advice, with a supplementary audit by the CAG?
new.x: Bodies like IFCI and Central Warehousing Corporation are audited by private auditors with CAG supplementary audit; LIC and RBI are wholly private, ONGC is audited directly.
new.angle: U0345 N1 bodies audited by private auditors vs CAG

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the separation of accounts from audit in 1976:
1. Union accounts are now compiled by the Controller General of Accounts.
2. The CAG still keeps most State accounts.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: After 1976 the CGA compiles Union accounts, while the CAG continues to keep most State accounts.
new.angle: U0345 #6/#15 separation of accounts from audit

new.s: By which method are the members of the Public Accounts Committee elected?
new.x: The 22 PAC members are elected every year by proportional representation through the single transferable vote.
new.angle: U0345 notes: PAC election by STV

new.s: Which office at the Union level corresponds to the Advocate General of a State?
new.x: The Advocate General (Art. 165) is the State counterpart of the Attorney General of India (Art. 76).

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Advocate General of a State:
1. His remuneration is determined by the Governor.
2. He has the right to vote in the State Legislature under Article 177.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Governor fixes his remuneration; Article 177 lets him speak in the State Legislature but not vote.
new.angle: U0346 #3/#12 Advocate General remuneration and rights

new.s: For at least how many years must a person have been a High Court judge to qualify as Attorney General of India?
new.x: The AG must be qualified to be a Supreme Court judge: a High Court judge for 5 years, an advocate of a High Court for 10 years, or a distinguished jurist.

new.s: Who is the present Solicitor General of India?
new.x: Tushar Mehta is the Solicitor General; he was reappointed for three years from 1 July 2026.

new.s: In which Part of the Constitution is the office of the Advocate General provided?
new.x: The Advocate General is under Article 165 in Part VI (the States); the Attorney General is under Article 76 in Part V.

new.s: Under which clause are the duties of the Advocate General of a State laid down?
new.x: Article 165(2) lays down his duties; 165(1) deals with appointment and 165(3) with tenure at the Governor's pleasure.

new.s: In which year was the Andhra Pradesh State Commission for SCs and STs created by a State Act?
new.x: The AP State Commission for SCs and STs was created by a 2003 State Act; it was later split into separate SC and ST commissions.
new.angle: U0347 #5 AP SC-ST Commission establishing Act

new.s: What is the legal status of the National Commission for Minorities?
o: Statutory body under the NCM Act
Executive body set up by a Cabinet resolution
new.x: The NCM is a statutory body under the NCM Act; it has no Article of the Constitution behind it.

new.s: Under which Ministry does the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities work?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
new.x: The Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities works under the Ministry of Minority Affairs, with headquarters in New Delhi.
new.angle: U0347 #4 Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities

new.s: Which Constitutional Amendment added Article 15(4), the first amendment on reservations?
new.x: Article 15(4) was added by the 1st Amendment, 1951, the first amendment on reservations.

new.s: Who is the present Chairperson of the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes?
new.x: Antar Singh Arya heads the NCST; Kishor Makwana heads the NCSC and Niranjan Jyoti the NCBC.

new.s: In which year was the Second Backward Classes Commission under B.P. Mandal appointed?
new.x: The Mandal Commission was appointed on 1 January 1979 by the Janata government.

new.s: Who was to head the statutory National Commission for Backward Classes set up under the 1993 Act?
o: A retired judge of the Supreme Court or a High Court
new.x: The statutory NCBC of 1993 had five members headed by a retired Supreme Court or High Court judge.

new.s: In January 2022, up to which date was the tenure of the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis extended?
new.x: In January 2022 the NCSK was extended for three years beyond 31 March 2022, that is, to 31 March 2025.
new.angle: U0348 #3 NCSK tenure extensions (APPSC PYQ ydf2903a3142)

new.s: What does Section 10 of the National Commission for Women Act, 1990 deal with?
new.x: Section 10 of the NCW Act lists the functions of the Commission, such as reviewing laws and looking into complaints.

new.s: Besides the Chairperson and the Member-Secretary, how many members does the National Commission for Women have?
new.x: The NCW has a Chairperson, five members (at least one SC and one ST) and a Member-Secretary.

new.s: Who among the following is NOT a member of the committee that recommends the Chairperson of a State Human Rights Commission?
new.x: The committee has the CM, Speaker, Home Minister and Leader of Opposition; the Governor only appoints.

new.s: In which year was a Minorities Commission first set up by a resolution of the Ministry of Home Affairs?
new.x: A Minorities Commission was set up by an MHA resolution in 1978; it became statutory under the NCM Act, 1992.

new.s:
Match the following:
List-I (Document)
A. CEDAW
B. Convention against Torture
C. UN Convention on the Rights of the Child
List-II (Year)
1. 1979
2. 1984
3. 1989
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
new.x: CEDAW was adopted in 1979, the Convention against Torture in 1984 and the UNCRC in 1989.

new.s: Who was the first Chairperson of the constitutional National Commission for Backward Classes (2019)?
new.x: Bhagwan Lal Sahni was the first Chairperson of the constitutional NCBC; Justice R.N. Prasad headed the statutory NCBC of 1993.
